Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroSpace Dynamics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroSpace Dynamics' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Vargas, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Strategy Officer; and Amanda Torres, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. AeroSpace Dynamics delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders.

We achieved record Q3 revenue of $2.85 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 8% sequentially from Q2. This beat our guidance midpoint by $150 million, driven by accelerated program ramps, favorable mix shifts, and robust demand across our Defense Systems and Aeronautics segments. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.12, surpassing consensus estimates of $1.05 by 7%, with GAAP EPS at $0.98. Our operating margin expanded 220 basis points to 13.8%, reflecting leverage from fixed-price development contracts transitioning to low-risk production phases, such as full-rate production on our next-gen hypersonic glide vehicle, the Aegis HyperStrike, now certified for U.S. Navy integration.

Our book-to-bill ratio remains strong at 1.3:1 for the quarter, pushing funded backlog to a record $52.4 billion, up 18% year-over-year. This provides multi-year visibility, with over 40% tied to international customers as part of our diversification strategy. Defense Systems, our largest unit at 58% of revenue, posted $1.65 billion, up 16% year-over-year, propelled by surging demand for precision-guided munitions amid ongoing conflicts. Shipments of our ViperStrike loitering munition exceeded 5,000 units, with export orders from Australia and Poland under AUKUS and NATO frameworks adding $450 million to the backlog. Margins there hit 15.2%, up from 13.9%, thanks to supply chain efficiencies post-2022 disruptions, including vendor consolidation that reduced lead times on rare earths by 35%.

Aeronautics delivered $1.02 billion, up 11% year-over-year, as commercial aftermarket services rebounded sharply. Our MRO contracts for Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo fleets generated $280 million, with utilization rates at 95%, reflecting pent-up demand from airlines like Delta and Emirates. On the defense side, progress on the NGAD digital engineering prototype advanced to TRL-7, securing a $2.1 billion award extension. Our Space & Advanced Technologies segment, at 14% of revenue with $380 million up 9% year-over-year, is a key growth driver, with revenue from resilient SATCOM payloads for the Space Development Agency's Tranche 2 Transport Layer hitting $150 million.

Regionally, U.S. revenue was 72% at $2.05 billion, bolstered by the FY24 NDAA's 5% topline increase to $886 billion. International sales jumped 22% to $680 million, led by the Middle East and Indo-Pacific. Key trends include geopolitical tailwinds, with global defense spending at $2.4 trillion per SIPRI, and our $450 million R&D investment focused on digital twins for sustainment, reducing life-cycle costs by 20%, and autonomy stacks for unmanned collaborative combat aircraft. Our October acquisition of Precision Munitions Tech for $1.2 billion accretes 15% to EPS in Year 1 and bolsters Stinger successor production. Partnerships with RTX on GhostWorks and Northrop on B-21 sustainment de-risk our runway, with ROIC at 18.2%, top-quartile in the sector.

We're particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to establish leadership in next-gen air dominance for future growth. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily. Before diving deeper into segment details, let me highlight our standout performance in major new contract awards and program wins, which underscore our leadership across the Aerospace & Defense spectrum amid escalating global geopolitical tensions and rising defense budgets.

In Q3, we secured $14.7 billion in new funded contract awards, bringing total backlog to a record $128 billion, up 22% year-over-year and representing over four years of revenue visibility. Our book-to-bill expanded to 1.35x, allowing us to pursue high-margin opportunities selectively. In our core Defense Electronics and Missiles segment, we captured two blockbuster awards totaling $6.2 billion. The standout is a $4.1 billion IDIQ contract from the U.S. Army for next-generation Precision Strike Missiles, including LRIP lots 3 through 7, incorporating advanced seeker technology for hypersonic glide vehicle defeat. We're using digital twin modeling and MBSE to compress timelines by 18 months. Complementing this, a $2.1 billion FMS award for PAC-3 MSE interceptors to Saudi Arabia and Poland, up 35% year-over-year in those regions due to missile threats.

In Fixed-Wing Aircraft and Sustainment, we notched a $3.8 billion sole-source follow-on with the U.S. Air Force for F-35 Block 4 modernization kits, including AESA radar upgrades and EW suites. Internationally, a $1.2 billion logistics support deal for the Royal Australian Air Force's F-35A fleet under AUKUS. In Space Systems, a pivotal $2.4 billion win with the NRO for Tranche 3 Tracking Layer under PWSA, involving 18 next-gen satellites with AI-driven EO/IR processing. We also added $450 million in commercial NewSpace wins, including propulsion for Blue Origin's New Glenn. On commercial aviation, amid Boeing's 737 MAX recovery, a $1.1 billion engine component deal for LEAP-1B nacelles.

These wins reflect our disciplined process, prioritizing >15% margins and discriminators like our hypersonics test bed and AI/ML predictive maintenance. International bookings hit 32% of total awards. Now, I'll turn it over to Michael for the financial details.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Johnathan. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $2.85 billion, representing a 14% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $1.12 adjusted. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $10 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year is raised: revenue to $11.0-$11.3 billion, EPS $4.45-$4.65, and FCF $2.1 billion. We are actively managing costs and investing in key growth initiatives, while returning capital through dividends and share repurchases.

Gross margin was 28%, operating income $393 million, free cash flow $1.2 billion. As we dive deeper, I'd like to spend time on our free cash flow generation and utilization, a cornerstone of our financial strength in this capital-intensive industry. FCF, cash from operations minus capex, was $1.2 billion for the quarter, up 33% from $900 million last year. Year-to-date, $3.5 billion, on track for $4.8 to $5.2 billion full year. This reflects maturity in high-margin sustainment and ramps on F-35 Lightning II and NGAD demonstrators.

Operating cash flow reached $2.1 billion, driven by collections on our $125 billion backlog, up 8% year-over-year. Missiles and Fire Control delivered $450 million from JASSM-ER and LRASM amid Ukraine and Indo-Pacific demand. Aeronautics F-35 lot deliveries hit 48 aircraft, our highest, with positive cash from Lot 15-17 fixed-price milestone payments. Days sales outstanding improved to 65 from 72, thanks to disciplined billing on FMS with UK, Japan, Poland. Capex was $900 million, within 3-4% of sales: 40% to advanced composites in Fort Worth for F-35 wings and NGAD, 30% to digital thread and MBSE reducing ECO costs 15-20%, balance to supply chain like dual-sourcing titanium.

FCF conversion exceeded 110% of adjusted net income, from 45% Aeronautics sustainment at 12-14% EBITDA. U.S. DoD 65%, international 35% standout with FMS up 25%, $2.5 billion new from Saudi THAAD and Australia Loyal Wingman under AUKUS, plus European Defence Fund hypersonics and $1.8 billion PACAF sustainment.

On utilization, of YTD $3.5 billion FCF: $1.2 billion net debt reduction to 1.8x leverage from 2.3x, $800 million dividends with 12th annual increase to $1.28/share at 1.8% yield, 55% payout; $1.0 billion repurchases under $4 billion authorization, retiring 2.5% shares at $420 average. Remainder $500 million reinvested: $300 million IR&D for directed energy weapons and space domain awareness aligning with Replicator, $200 million M&A like hypersonics startup for Glide Phase Interceptor.

Forward, FCF margins to 12-13% FY25 from F-35 scaling to 156 annually, JMIC space wins, EDT digitizing 80% factories by 2026. Risks like rare earth inflation, Huntsville labor, but $10 billion cash, $3 billion revolver strong.

Turning to program margins and cost performance, which reflect portfolio resilience amid supply chain headwinds. Consolidated A&D margins expanded 120 basis points to 12.8%, exceeding 12.0-12.5% guidance, third straight quarter up from 11.6%. Trailing 12-month 12.4%, nearing 13-14% target. CPI 1.05, SPI 1.02, favorable $285 million variances or 2.1% revenue from labor productivity, material reductions. Backlog $148 billion, 65% production.

Inflation navigated: labor 4.2%, titanium/composites 8-10%. Defense Fixed-Wing 14.2% up 150 bps, F-35 subcontracts 16.5%, CPI 1.12 from digital thread cutting labor 18%, $450 million ECRs offsetting inflation. NGAD EAC $75 million but stabilized. Missiles & Hypersonics 15.8% up 80 bps, CPI 1.08, $180 million savings vertical integration SRM. Space 11.5% down 50 bps from delays, but SPI 1.05, recovery via reusables. Commercial 9.8% rebound, CPI 1.03, $110 million localization.

Savings $620 million YTD: MBSE/digital twins $150 million, lean robotics labor CPI 1.15, dual-sourcing 85% Tier 1, 7% material deflation. EACs reaffirmed 92%. Geopolitics: DoD supplements, GCAP uplift. Affordability by design, IDIQs, R&D 6.2% for CCA.

On defense budget outlook, FY25 request $849.8 billion, up 1%, procurement +4.2%, R&D +2.1%; NDAA $895 billion. Tailwinds hypersonics, CCA, JADC2. U.S. 72% backlog: F-35 $80 million/jet, B-21 LRIP $1.2 billion share, NGAD $2.8 billion MBSE ahead. Europe NATO €380 billion, $4.2 billion FMS PAC-3/NASAMS. Asia AUKUS/Quad $3.1 billion, GPI CDR. Missiles/Space revenue +18%, margins +150 bps. R&D $450 million DEW/quantum. Risks CRs, inflation, but $1.2 billion savings buffer. Raised FY25: revenue $28.5-$29.5 billion +6%, margins 12.0-12.5%, FCF $3.8 billion.

Finally, on commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery trajectory, Q3 deliveries 380 units, up 25% YoY, strongest since 2019, book-to-bill 1.4x, backlog $520 billion or 5,200 aircraft. Narrowbodies 280 (74%), widebodies 100. North America 45% to Delta/United, Europe 20% Lufthansa/easyJet, Asia 25% ANA/IndiGo, China 8%, Middle East 12%. Supply chain: dual CFM LEAP, titanium +35%, suppliers 95% OTD. Ramps: 42 PPM MAX to 52, AI maintenance -28% defects, CFRP +40%. Defense synergies 15% margins. 2024 1,550 deliveries +18%, 2025 1,800.

Lisa Vargas:
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've seen significant improvements in supply chain management, increasing production rates on key programs. We're investing in automation and digital technologies for efficiency and cost reduction, including AeroForge vertical integration producing 70% aerostructures in-house to mitigate tariffs and delays. Our factories are at 95% on-time delivery, with productivity savings buffering inflation.

Dr. Elena Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. On the technology front, we're advancing next-generation propulsion systems and directed energy weapons, like our 300kW solid-state laser passing Navy HELIOS trials. These give us a competitive edge, with HAWC-derived hypersonics entering LRIP, MQ-Next CCA for manned-unmanned teaming, and Orion/LEO hardening. We're pioneering digital twins, MBSE, and AI autonomy.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Elena. Strategically, we're evaluating acquisitions complementing our portfolio, like Precision Munitions Tech and hypersonics tuck-ins, expanding hypersonics TAM to $15 billion by 2030. New models capture hypersonics, CCA, DEW via Replicator, JADC2. Priorities: production ramps like LRASM to 650 units, F-35 Lots 16-18; next-gen R&D $1.2 billion hypersonics/autonomy/space; supply chain 85% multi-sourced, workforce upskilling. Q1 '25 revenue $8.1-8.4 billion +9-12%, EPS $1.85-1.95; FY25 $34-35 billion +10-13%, margins 13.5-14.0%, FCF $3.2-3.5 billion, $1 billion buybacks, 10% dividend hike.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from David Ramirez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Ramirez:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the major new contract awards, particularly the F-35 and space wins?

Johnathan Reyes:
Certainly, David. The $3.8 billion F-35 Block 4 sole-source builds on our incumbency with AESA and EW upgrades for Lot 15-18 ramps, forecasting 15% revenue uplift. The $2.4 billion NRO Tranche 3 leverages our SDA heritage with AI EO/IR and OISLs for SDA, addressing Space Force priorities amid $30 billion procurement.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about free cash flow utilization and how you're balancing debt reduction with M&A?

Michael Chen:
Emily, our discipline allocates YTD $3.5 billion FCF with $1.2 billion deleveraging to 1.8x, $800 million dividends, $1 billion buybacks opportunistically. The $500 million remainder funds IR&D like Replicator-aligned attritables and tuck-ins like the hypersonics startup, mirroring sector playbooks to grow hypersonics TAM while maintaining investment-grade strength.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Hale with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Hale:
Regarding the commercial aircraft recovery trajectory and supply chain risks?

Lisa Vargas:
Tom, deliveries at 380 units reflect stabilization, with dual-sourcing LEAP/GTF and titanium fabs hitting 95% OTD. We're targeting 50 PPM sustainably by 2025, leveraging defense tech transfers for fly-by-wire and materials, hedging with freighter backlogs amid FAA lifts and +9% RPK growth.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
